lessons.title: Read an SOP before using it
objectives: Check scope authority and version before following instructions.
explanation: A standard operating procedure describes a repeatable task, its scope, responsible roles, prerequisites, steps and required evidence. A useful SOP also identifies exceptions, stop conditions and related documents. Standardization reduces avoidable variation only when the procedure is appropriate and current.

Before use, check document ID, version, approval, effective date and applicability to the actual equipment and site. An attractive draft is not an approved procedure. If two versions conflict, pause the affected task and ask the authorized owner to identify the current version. The generic templates in this course are Draft and must not be used as official AITS instructions.

lessons.title: Evidence and deviations
objectives: Record actual results and disclose departures from the plan.
explanation: Evidence connects a requirement to an observed result. Record what was checked, the method, time, relevant identifier and result. “Done” alone is weak evidence when the next reviewer cannot tell which requirement was tested. Do not fabricate a photo, measurement or signature.

A deviation is a departure from the applicable requirement or planned process. Record the difference and its impact; seek authorized disposition instead of silently changing the procedure. Depending on the risk, the task may need to pause. Preserve the original evidence and record any correction with traceable history. A failed check can be useful information when it is reported honestly.
lessons.example: The required playback test was not performed because access was unavailable. Record “not tested, access pending,” rather than a pass.
lessons.exercise: Rewrite “all OK” into a test record with an unresolved item.
lessons.model_response: Device C2 live view verified at 14:00 under the agreed scene. Playback not tested; authorized access pending. Review requested before acceptance.
lessons.thai_summary: บันทึกสิ่งที่ตรวจจริง วิธีตรวจ เวลา และผล งานที่ยังไม่ทดสอบต้องไม่บันทึกว่าผ่าน
lessons.summary: Record method and observed result Not tested is not passed Keep deviations visible

lessons.title: Quality assurance and completion review
objectives: Distinguish process prevention from checking a finished result.
explanation: Quality assurance builds reliable methods, training and review into the work. Quality control checks outputs against defined requirements. Both are useful: a final inspection can detect a defect, while a better preparation process may prevent it. The ISO overview supports this general distinction; this course makes no claim that AITS holds a particular certification.

For a completion review, compare the approved scope with evidence and open issues. Confirm that required tests have results, exceptions have an authorized disposition and the handover is understandable. Record recurring problems for improvement without changing a controlled procedure on your own. A customer signature alone does not erase an unresolved safety or technical issue.
lessons.example: Repeated wrong device quantities suggest a preparation and reconciliation problem, even if a final count catches each error.
lessons.exercise: Propose one preventive process check and one final output check for an installation kit.
lessons.model_response: Preventive: reconcile approved scope and picking list before dispatch. Output: verify actual kit quantities and condition against the list.
key_points: Close work against evidence and scope

lessons.title: AI checks and human authority
objectives: Use AI feedback as practice support with source and approval controls.
explanation: An AI can help compare a written report with a checklist, ask missing questions and explain a training example. It may still misunderstand images, omit context or produce an unsupported answer. It cannot verify hidden physical conditions from a photograph, grant approval or turn a draft SOP into company policy.

Before accepting AI feedback, inspect the cited source, version, approval and applicability. Keep company-authoritative retrieval restricted to approved company records. Draft and hypothetical items may support clearly labeled practice, but not a policy answer. Do not submit secrets or unnecessary personal data. An AI practice score is formative feedback; official competency assessment requires the company’s approved human-led process.
lessons.example: An AI says a camera installation passes from one photograph. Ask which requirements and evidence were checked; unresolved physical tests remain unresolved.
lessons.exercise: Write an AI response to “What is AITS’s travel allowance?” when no approved policy is available.
lessons.model_response: I do not have verified AITS travel-allowance terms. Please ask HR or the responsible company department for the current approved policy.
